title: Hang up a desk phone: set the handset back so each end sits in its own cradle cup
instruction: The call is over. Hang up: put the handset back on the phone so each end sits in its own cup of the cradle and the hook switch is pressed down, then let go. Don't shove the phone about.
context: Everyone has hung up a desk phone; for office clerks and receptionists (SOC 43-9061 and 43-4171, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) it is dozens of times a day, and a handset not fully down leaves the line busy, so callers get an engaged tone. What makes it hard is that it is a double insertion with a switch: two pads must drop into two separate cups at once (8 mm clear across, 6 mm at each end), so the handset must be level and square (6 degrees, 3 degrees) after a quarter turn in the hand, and it seats only one way round (the mouthpiece end is longer). Its weight must also press the spring hook switch 2 mm to close the line, and it cannot be fixed by shoving the loose, light phone. The desk is crowded: a monitor stands behind the phone and a pen pot beside it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the desk top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. Four things. (1) Phone base: charcoal ABS shell on rubber feet, 200 mm (x) by 240 mm (y), 55 mm high, 1.10 kg, loose on the desk, centred at x 300 mm, y 0. Its top has two rectangular cups sunk 10 mm, with vertical walls and flat floors: the earpiece cup, 58 mm (y) by 60 mm (x), centred y +72 mm, and the mouthpiece cup, 82 mm (y) by 68 mm (x), centred y -67 mm (both at x 300 mm). Between them the top is flat (y -26 to +43 mm). On that flat, at y +8 mm, x 300 mm, stands the hook switch: a round plunger 14 mm across, 8 mm proud of the top (63 mm over the desk), spring-loaded at 200 N/m, with 8 mm of travel. (2) Handset: charcoal ABS, 0.17 kg, 197 mm long, one rigid body: two square-edged end pads and a round handle. An earpiece pad 46 mm long by 44 mm wide by 28 mm tall; a mouthpiece pad 70 mm long by 52 mm wide by 28 mm tall, its centre 139 mm from the earpiece pad's; and a round handle 130 mm long and 34 mm across joining them (its centre 77 mm from the earpiece pad's centre and 62 mm from the mouthpiece pad's, all three centred across the width), its underside 14 mm above the pads' flat bottoms (so it arches clear of the desk and its top is 48 mm over the pad bottoms). The pad bottoms are what go in the cups, 8 mm clear each side across it (x) and 6 mm at each end (y); the mouthpiece pad is longer than the earpiece cup, so the handset seats one way round only. It starts face down (pad bottoms on the desk), its long axis along x, the earpiece pad centred at x 392 mm and the mouthpiece pad at x 253 mm, both at y -220 mm; the gripper opening is 94 mm and the handle is held across its 34 mm. (3) Monitor (fixed): black plastic flat panel 25 mm thick, 520 mm wide (y), 310 mm tall, its lower edge 120 mm over the desk, on a 160 mm (x) by 240 mm (y) by 20 mm foot with a 30 by 60 by 130 mm neck, foot centred at x 560 mm, y 0. (4) Pen pot (fixed): blue plastic cylinder, 80 mm across, 100 mm tall, centred at x 360 mm, y +175 mm. There is no cord. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Read every control step; faults are remembered for the whole trial. How the handset is tilted on the way is not judged, only where it ends. All pad and phone readings are in the phone's own frame (x across it, y along it), so a nudged phone is judged fairly. 'Pad in its cup': the pad's four bottom corners inside its own cup's rectangle (0.5 mm allowed) and from 2 mm below to 6 mm above the cup floor (earpiece pad in the earpiece cup, mouthpiece pad in the mouthpiece cup). 'Pad resting on the phone': its four bottom corners over the phone's top outline and from 2 mm below to 14 mm above the cup floors (down in a cup, or up on the flat top, which is 10 mm higher). 'Seated': both pads in their own cups with every pad corner from 2 mm below to 3 mm above the floor; the handset's long axis within 6 degrees of the phone's (plan view); its underside within 3 degrees of level against the phone; and the hook plunger pressed down 2 mm or more (the line is closed). 'Hands off': on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the handset and the phone, and in that second the handset and the phone each move under 5 mm and turn under 5 degrees (visible motion; the GPU demo ran at 0.0 mm and 0.0 degrees). Faults, any one at any moment: the handset or the phone more than 10 mm below the desk top (fallen off); the phone more than 8 mm from its starting place or tilted more than 3 degrees. Score: 1.0 seated and hands off; 0.5 one or both pads in their own cups and both pads resting on the phone, not seated (for instance one end up on a cup's rim, or both in but the plunger not down), hands off; 0.25 both pads resting on the phone and neither in its own cup (lying across the top, or turned end for end), hands off; 0 otherwise, and 0 after any fault or whenever the hands are not off. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: pad height, 2 mm and 3 mm feeler gauges under the pad bottoms; pad in cup, a 0.5 mm feeler between pad and cup wall; heading, a try-square on the phone's long side (6 degrees is 20 mm over the handset's length); level, a phone level on the handle (3 degrees); hook, a depth gauge on the plunger or the phone's line lamp (2 mm); hands off, a 30 mm spacer block and a ruler or grid sheet under both parts (5 mm and 5 degrees); phone shift, an 8 mm outline taped round its feet; fall, by eye and a ruler.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The coiled cord is left out: a real cord adds a tether and drag, so this task isolates the seating, the quarter turn and the switch press, not cord handling. The handset is two square-edged pads and a round handle (real ones are moulded in one curve). The phone is a slab with two cups and the hook switch, no keypad or display; cup walls are vertical (real cradles have lead-ins). Plunger: 200 N/m spring, 8 mm travel. Friction 0.45 handset, 1.0 phone feet (est).
reset_notes: Lay the handset face down (pad bottoms on the desk), long axis along x, the earpiece pad centred at x 392 mm and the mouthpiece pad at x 253 mm, both at y -220 mm. Stand the phone on its feet centred at x 300 mm, y 0, plunger up and free. Monitor foot at x 560 mm, y 0; pen pot at x 360 mm, y +175 mm. Nothing is consumed.
